answer: An agent archive storing violet and saffron crop images can pay for storage using proofs of replication. Each paid copy has a distinct encoding tied to its commitment; a public randomness beacon selects blocks to prove under a deadline too short to reconstruct a copy. A global registry prevents the same commitment earning through multiple names. More aliases earn nothing unless the operator provides additional encoded storage and stays online. The attack therefore costs disk capacity and bandwidth; this needs a sound replication proof, not ordinary file hashes.
